topic.title: Neural Operators and Learned Physical Simulation
topic.area: Continuous Models and Scientific Machine Learning
topic.overview: Learned simulators approximate how physical systems evolve, potentially replacing expensive numerical computations. This topic includes graph-based dynamics, neural operators, mesh-independent representations, and models shared across physical domains. Effective learning must respect spatial relationships and temporal evolution rather than merely fit isolated field values.
topic.whyItMatters: Fast predictions are valuable for animation, engineering, and repeated simulation, but small local errors can grow during long rollouts. Generalization across meshes, geometries, and boundary conditions is therefore as important as accuracy on familiar snapshots. Numerical structure offers constraints that can improve stability and transfer.
topic.evolution: NeuroAnimator in 1998 learns to emulate physics-based animation models from simulated trajectories. Later representatives develop interaction networks and operators for partial differential equations. Recent work scales transformer solvers; a 2026 study combines neighborhood-level prediction, temporal correction, and geometric biases to improve accuracy and stability across several simulation architectures.
openQuestions: Which conservation and consistency constraints are essential for reliable long-horizon simulation?
How can operator models transfer to unfamiliar geometries without extensive new simulation data?
